Study tips

# How to use mock tests and mistakes to prepare for your learner test

By BlueOrbit (https://blue0orbit.github.io/learners-test-australia/about.html) · Published 30 September 2026 · Last updated: 30 September 2026 · 4 min read

Summary

Mock tests work best when you sit them like the real test and then study your mistakes. Know your mistake budget: 1 in the NSW DKT road safety section, 3 in NSW general knowledge, 7 in the Victorian in-person test, 1 in Queensland's giving-way section, 2 in its road rules section and 3 in the PrepL final test. Then read each explanation, look up the rule and come back to the question a few days later.

## What is a mistake budget?

Every learner knowledge test has a pass mark, and the gap between the number of questions and the pass mark is your mistake budget: how many you can get wrong and still pass. Where a test has sections, each section has its own budget, and you can't borrow from one to cover another.

Mistake budgets by test (formats as published, checked 30 September 2026)

| Test | Section | Questions | Pass mark | Mistakes allowed |
| NSW DKT | General knowledge | 15 | 12 | 3 |
| Road safety | 30 | 29 | 1 |
| VIC Learner permit test (in person) | All questions | 32 | 25 | 7 |
| QLD Written road rules test | Giving way | 10 | 9 | 1 |
| Road rules and licence requirements | 20 | 18 | 2 |
| QLD PrepL final test | All questions | 30 | 27 | 3 |

Look at where the budget is tight. One mistake in NSW road safety or Queensland giving way is all you get. That is where a mock test tells you the most.

## When should you start doing mock tests?

Not on day one. A mock test measures what you know; it isn't the best way to learn it. Start by reading your state's handbook a chapter at a time and answering practice questions on each topic. In the app, a 12-question quick check finds your starting point, and the daily plan mixes reviews, mistakes and new questions.

Once you've worked through every topic at least once, start sitting full mock tests. From then on, alternate: mock test, fix the mistakes, practise, and mock test again.

## How do you sit a mock test like the real thing?

- Find a quiet spot and set aside enough time to finish in one go.
- No notes, no handbook and no looking things up. The point is to find the gaps.
- Answer every question, and flag the ones you're unsure of to review afterwards.
- Read the whole question and every option before choosing. Many wrong options are tempting because they are almost right.

In the NSW mock, the test ends where the real DKT would, as soon as passing is no longer possible, and you can choose to keep practising the remaining questions. That early stop is a useful jolt: it shows exactly how little room there is in the road safety section.

## What should you do with your mistakes?

Your mistakes are the most valuable part of a mock test. For each one:

- Read the explanation and the rule it comes from. In the app every answer shows the handbook page or road rule.
- Work out why you got it wrong. Did you not know the rule, misread the question, or mix it up with a similar rule?
- Look it up. Reading the handbook page puts the rule in context and often clears up neighbouring rules too.
- Come back to it later. Answering it again a few days later, rather than straight away, is what makes it stick.

Don't ignore your lucky guesses either. A correct answer you guessed is a mistake waiting to happen. The app asks “How sure were you?” after each answer (knew it, unsure or guessed) and uses your reply to decide when to show the question again.

## How should you read your results?

Look at each section against its own pass line, not just your total. A score of 40 out of 45 in the NSW DKT sounds comfortable, but if 2 of those 5 mistakes were in road safety, it is a fail. In the app, results show every section against its pass line, and the Today screen shows your weakest topic.

Over time, the pass-chance estimate combines your recent answers into a single number. Treat it as a guide, not a guarantee: it is based on practice questions, and the official test is set by your state. Premium adds a forecast for each section, which helps when one section is holding you back.

## How many mock tests should you do?

There is no magic number. A better target is consistency: pass several mock tests in a row with a little room to spare in every section, especially the tight ones. If you pass one and fail the next, keep going.

Aim to understand the rules rather than memorise answers. Our questions are original, not the official ones, so recognising a question won't help you in the real test; knowing the rule will. In the free version you get one mock test a day, plus another each time you choose to watch a short ad. Premium makes them unlimited.

## Which traps catch people out?

- Other states' numbers. Learning from a mix of sources can teach you the wrong figures. Supervised hours are a classic: NSW asks under-25s for 120 hours including 20 at night; Victoria asks for 120 hours, 20 or more after dark, if you'll be under 21 at your licence test; Queensland asks under-25s for 100 hours including 10 at night.
- Old rules. Rules change. Check that what you're learning matches the current handbook and your state's website.
- Rushing the easy ones. Most mistakes on questions you know come from reading too fast.

Ready to start? See the practice pages for NSW (https://blue0orbit.github.io/learners-test-australia/nsw-dkt-practice-test.html), VIC (https://blue0orbit.github.io/learners-test-australia/vic-learner-permit-test-practice.html) and QLD (https://blue0orbit.github.io/learners-test-australia/qld-learner-test-practice.html).

## Check the official source

- NSW Driver Knowledge Test (nsw.gov.au) (official website) (https://www.nsw.gov.au/driving-boating-and-transport/driving-nsw/driver-and-rider-licences/driver-licences/driver-licence-tests/driver-knowledge-test)
- Victorian learner permit test (VicRoads) (official website) (https://www.vicroads.vic.gov.au/ls-and-ps/getting-your-ls/learner-permit-test)
- Queensland driver tests (qld.gov.au) (official website) (https://www.qld.gov.au/transport/licensing/getting/tests)
- Queensland PrepL (qld.gov.au) (official website) (https://www.qld.gov.au/transport/licensing/getting/learner/prepl/prepl/prepl-online-learning-and-assessment)

Rules and test formats change. We checked these pages on 30 September 2026; the official website is always the final word.

Hazard perception

# Hazard perception test: what it is in NSW, VIC and QLD

By BlueOrbit (https://blue0orbit.github.io/learners-test-australia/about.html) · Published 30 September 2026 · Last updated: 30 September 2026 · 4 min read

Summary

Hazard perception is the skill of spotting possible dangers early, judging how risky they are and responding in time. In NSW, Victoria and Queensland you sit a hazard perception test (HPT) during your learner period, after the knowledge test and before the practical driving test. When you can sit it and how long a pass lasts differ by state. Facts as checked on 30 September 2026.

## What is hazard perception?

Hazard perception is the skill of spotting possible dangers on the road, judging how risky they are, predicting what might happen, and responding in time. Victoria's Road to Solo Driving handbook stresses that it is not the same as quick reactions: young drivers often react fast but are slower to anticipate. It grows only with plenty of varied driving experience, and the aim is that most situations on the road don't take you by surprise.

Hazards are anything that could lead to a crash: vehicles ahead, behind, beside you or in side streets, a truck double-parked, trains, pedestrians, bicycle riders, weather, potholes, heavy traffic, tight curves and crests you can't see over.

## Where does the hazard perception test fit in each state?

In all three states the hazard perception test (HPT) comes during your learner period, after the knowledge test and before the practical driving test.

Hazard perception test by state (checked 30 September 2026)

| State | When you can sit it | How long a pass lasts |
| NSW | If you are under 25, after at least 10 months on your Ls | 15 months, for the driving test |
| VIC | From 17 years 11 months, with a current Victorian learner permit | Pass the drive test within 12 months, or sit the HPT again |
| QLD | After holding your learner licence for at least 6 months; required for every car learner, whatever their age | You pass it once |

## What should you know about the HPT in NSW?

In NSW the Hazard Perception Test is the second of three tests: the DKT gets you your Ls, the HPT comes during your learner period, and the driving test gets you your P1 licence. If you are under 25, you can only sit it after at least 10 months on your learner licence, and your pass stays valid for 15 months for the driving test. The NSW Government's HPT page explains the current format and how to book.

## What should you know about the HPT in Victoria?

In Victoria you must pass the Hazard Perception Test before the drive test. You can sit it from 17 years 11 months if you hold a current Victorian learner permit. VicRoads describes it as 25 short video clips, taking up to 45 minutes, in which you choose whether to slow down, stop or keep going. After you pass, you have 12 months to pass the drive test; otherwise you sit the HPT again.

## What should you know about the HPT in Queensland?

Since 1 July 2021 every car learner in Queensland, of any age, must pass the hazard perception test before the practical test. You can sit it after holding your learner licence for at least 6 months, and your logbook doesn't need to be finished first. It is done online only, not at service centres, using computer-generated 3D video clips of situations that crash data shows are hard for new drivers, and you only need to pass it once. The fee was $42.70 as at 1 July 2026. If you turn up to the practical test without an HPT pass, the test is cancelled and the fee isn't refunded.

## How do you build hazard perception skill?

Mostly by driving, with a supervisor, in as many different conditions as you can. The Victorian handbook's advice applies everywhere:

- Scan the whole scene. Keep looking far ahead, to both sides and in your mirrors, rather than staring at the car in front.
- Know your blind spots. Every car has areas no mirror shows, however well the mirrors are set. Head-check with a quick glance over your shoulder before changing lanes, merging, pulling out, reversing or overtaking.
- Practise in variety: at night, in the wet, in busy and quiet traffic, on roads with different speed limits, and on sealed and gravel surfaces.
- Drive little and often. Frequent short drives of 10 minutes to an hour are worth more than a few long ones, especially early on.

The supervised hours each state asks for exist partly for this reason: NSW asks under-25s for 120 hours, Victoria asks for 120 hours if you'll be under 21 at your licence test, and Queensland asks under-25s for 100 hours.

## Can an app help with hazard perception?

An app can't replace time behind the wheel, but it can help you practise the thinking. Learners Test Australia has illustrated traffic scenes, drawn from above, where you tap the hazard you should be ready for and then read why it matters: a person waiting between parked cars, a ball on the road with a child nearby, a parked car signalling to pull out, or a kangaroo beside a country road at dusk. A few sample scenes are free, and Premium unlocks the full set. Each state also has a guide to its HPT.

The scenes are still images for practice. They are not a copy of any official test, which uses video clips. For the knowledge test side, see our mock test guide (https://blue0orbit.github.io/learners-test-australia/blog/how-to-use-mock-tests-and-mistakes.html) and the feature tour (https://blue0orbit.github.io/learners-test-australia/features.html).

## Check the official source

- Hazard Perception Test (nsw.gov.au) (official website) (https://www.nsw.gov.au/driving-boating-and-transport/driving-nsw/driver-and-rider-licences/driver-licences/driver-licence-tests/hazard-perception-test)
- Hazard perception test (VicRoads) (official website) (https://www.vicroads.vic.gov.au/ls-and-ps/getting-your-ps/hazard-perception-test)
- Driver tests, written and online (qld.gov.au) (official website) (https://www.qld.gov.au/transport/licensing/getting/tests)
- Driver licence progression (qld.gov.au) (official website) (https://www.qld.gov.au/transport/licensing/driver-licensing/applying/driver-licence-progression)

Rules and test formats change. We checked these pages on 30 September 2026; the official website is always the final word.

About

# About Learners Test Australia and how we make our questions

Who makes the app, why it exists, and the process behind every question.

Last updated: 30 September 2026

## Who makes Learners Test Australia?

Learners Test Australia is made by BlueOrbit, an independent app developer. BlueOrbit is not a driving school or a government agency, and the app has no connection with any licensing authority. You can reach us at blue0orbit@gmail.com.

## Why a state-by-state learner test app?

Each state runs its own knowledge test with its own format, pass marks and licensing rules. A question bank that mixes them up teaches the wrong numbers: the supervised hours, plate rules and alcohol limits for new drivers are not the same everywhere. So the app has one profile per state, and each profile follows that state's handbook, test format and rules.

## How are the questions made and checked?

-

### A coverage map for each state

We list every fact the official material tests, using the current handbook, the official test pages, the official practice tests (only to see which facts get tested) and the road rules legislation. Each fact records its source and the date it was checked.

-

### Original questions

Every question is written in our own words to test one fact from the map, with wrong options based on common misunderstandings. No official question, answer option, handbook sentence or image is reproduced, and we don't paraphrase official question banks.

-

### A source and a review date on every question

Each question carries the handbook page or road rule it comes from and the date it was last verified. The launch packs were checked on 30 September 2026.

-

### The current rule wins

Where an older official source differs from the current rule, the question follows the current rule. Facts we couldn't confirm from a current official source are flagged for manual checking rather than turned into questions.

-

### Original artwork

Road signs, markings and diagrams are redrawn from written descriptions, not traced from official artwork.

## Which official sources are the questions checked against?

| State | Handbook and edition | Also checked against |
| NSW | Road User Handbook, edition 02/2026 | NSW Road Rules 2014 and NSW Government licence and test pages |
| VIC | Road to Solo Driving, April 2023 edition | Road Safety Road Rules 2017 and current Transport Victoria and VicRoads pages |
| QLD | Your keys to driving in Queensland, No. 19 (November 2022) | The Queensland Road Rules Regulation in force from 31 August 2026 and current Queensland Government pages |

Where a handbook is older than the current rules (for example, Queensland's 2022 handbook predates the 2026 e-scooter and e-bike changes), the current official pages and legislation decide the answer.

## Attribution

Queensland road rules content is based on content from the Queensland Legislation website at 30 September 2026 (CC BY 4.0). Queensland Government web pages are © The State of Queensland (Department of Transport and Main Roads), CC BY 4.0. Transport Victoria web pages are licensed under CC BY 4.0, except images and branding. We restate facts in our own words, reproduce no text, logos or images, and none of these sources endorses the app or this website.

## Independence

Learners Test Australia is an independent study app. It is not affiliated with, or endorsed by, Transport for NSW, Service NSW, VicRoads, Transport Victoria, Queensland TMR or any government agency.

## About this website

This site uses no cookies, analytics or trackers and loads nothing from third parties. See the privacy policy (https://blue0orbit.github.io/learners-test-australia/privacy-policy.html#website).

## At a glance

- App: Learners Test Australia: DKT
- Developer: BlueOrbit
- Platform: Android 8.0 or later
- States: NSW, VIC, QLD
- Languages: 5
- Price: free, optional A$5.99 Premium
- Contact: blue0orbit@gmail.com

# Privacy Policy

How the Learners Test Australia app handles your information, and a note on this website.

Last updated: 30 September 2026

App: Learners Test Australia: DKT (Android) · Developer: BlueOrbit · Contact: blue0orbit@gmail.com

This is the same privacy policy shown in the app (Settings → Privacy policy).

## Overview

Learners Test Australia is an independent study app that helps you prepare for an Australian learner driver knowledge test. It is not affiliated with any government, transport or licensing agency.

This policy explains what the app collects, why, and the choices you have. Questions: blue0orbit@gmail.com.

## Information we collect

Account: when you sign in with Google, Facebook or email, we receive your name and email address.

Study data: your answers, completed practice sessions and mock tests, saved questions and the state you study for. This is stored on your device and in your account so it follows you to a new phone. Your test date and reminder settings stay on your device.

If you allow “Help improve the app”: anonymous usage statistics and crash reports (device model, Android version, app version, screens used).

Ads: the free version shows ads. Ad providers may use your device’s advertising ID. Where the law requires it (for example in the EEA and UK), Google asks for your consent first, and you can change it in Settings.

## How we use your data

We use your data to:

- Create your account and keep your progress in sync
- Build your daily plan, reviews and pass-chance estimate
- Send study reminders and announcements, if you turn them on
- Send tips and offers by email, only if you opt in (unsubscribe any time)
- Show ads in the free version
- Fix crashes and improve the app, if you allow it

We never sell your personal information.

## Third-party services

The app uses these services, each with its own privacy policy:

- Google Firebase — sign-in, cloud storage of progress, analytics, crash reports, push messages and remote settings
- Google AdMob — banner ads (free version)
- Unity Ads — optional rewarded video ads (free version)
- Google User Messaging Platform — ad consent where required
- Google Play Billing — the Premium purchase (we never see your payment details)
- Facebook Login — optional sign-in

## Data protection & retention

Your data is shared only with the providers above, and only as needed to run the app. Data is sent over encrypted connections, and your cloud data can only be read by your own account.

We keep your data while your account exists. Delete your account in Settings and your cloud progress and profile are deleted straight away; copies in the providers’ backups are removed within 30 days. You can also email us to ask for deletion.

## Your rights

Australia: we handle personal information under the Australian Privacy Principles (Privacy Act 1988). You can ask to access or correct your information, or complain, by emailing us. If you are not satisfied with our response you can contact the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (oaic.gov.au (https://www.oaic.gov.au/)).

EEA and UK: you have rights to access, correct, delete, restrict and port your data and to object to processing. We rely on your consent for analytics, marketing email and personalised ads, and on our contract with you to run your account.

Children: the app is for people preparing for a learner licence, usually 15 and over. It is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect their data.

Changes: if we change this policy in an important way, we will tell you in the app first.

## Contact

Privacy questions, data requests or complaints:

Email: blue0orbit@gmail.com

We aim to reply within 5 business days.

## This website

This section is about the website you are reading now (blue0orbit.github.io/learners-test-australia), not the app.

- No cookies. The website sets no cookies and stores nothing in your browser (no local storage or similar).
- No analytics or trackers. There are no analytics, advertising, tracking pixels or social media widgets.
- Nothing loaded from third parties. Fonts, images, styles and the one small script (it opens and closes the menu on small screens) are all served from this website itself.
- Hosting. The site is hosted on GitHub Pages. GitHub says it logs the IP address of visitors to GitHub Pages sites for security purposes (see About GitHub Pages (https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/about-github-pages)). We don't use those logs, and the site has no analytics of its own.
- Email. If you email us, we use your message and email address to reply to you.

See also the cookie policy (https://blue0orbit.github.io/learners-test-australia/cookies.html) and how to delete your account (https://blue0orbit.github.io/learners-test-australia/account-deletion.html).

# Delete your Learners Test Australia account and data

Last updated: 30 September 2026

App: Learners Test Australia: DKT (Android, package com.blueorbit.learnerstestau)
Developer: BlueOrbit
Contact: blue0orbit@gmail.com

You can delete your Learners Test Australia account and the data linked to it at any time, either in the app or by email. Uninstalling the app does not delete your account.

## Option 1: delete your account in the app

- Open Learners Test Australia and sign in to the account you want to delete.
- Tap the Settings (gear) icon at the top of the Today, Practice, Tests or Progress tab.
- Scroll to Account and tap Delete account (“Removes your account and all saved progress”).
- Read the message and tap Delete to confirm. This can't be undone.
- If you haven't signed in recently, the app deletes your progress first and then asks you to sign in again. Sign in and repeat this step to finish deleting the account itself.

When it's done, the app shows “Your account has been deleted.”

## Option 2: ask us by email

If you can't use the app (for example, you no longer have the phone), email blue0orbit@gmail.com from the email address of your account, with the subject “Delete my account”. We may reply to that address to confirm the request before deleting. We aim to reply within 5 business days.

You can also email us if you want particular data deleted without deleting your whole account.

## What is deleted

- Your account (your sign-in).
- Your profile: your name and email address.
- Your progress in every state: answers, completed practice sessions and mock tests, and saved questions.
- Your email preferences.

Your cloud progress and profile are deleted straight away. Copies in our service providers’ backups are removed within 30 days.

## What is kept

- Premium purchases. A Premium purchase belongs to the Google account that bought it, and purchase records are kept by Google Play under its own policies, not by us. We never see or store your payment details. If you later sign in again with the same Google account, Premium is still available. Deleting your account does not refund a purchase, except where required by law.
- Settings stored only on your phone. Your test date and reminder settings stay on your device. They are removed when you uninstall the app or clear its storage in Android settings.

More detail is in the privacy policy (https://blue0orbit.github.io/learners-test-australia/privacy-policy.html#data-protection-and-retention).
